# CF-004: The tunnel token is not a command line argument

- **Group:** Cloudflare Tunnel
- **Severity when it fails:** moderate
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

A token passed as a command line flag is visible to every local user in ps, in the systemd unit file, and in docker inspect output, which ends up in logs, bug reports and support chats. Anyone with the token can run a connector for your tunnel. stackward only records that the flag is present, never the value.

## Verify by hand

```sh
ps -o args= -C cloudflared | grep -c -- --token
```

## How to fix it

Pass the token as TUNNEL_TOKEN from a root only env file (or a credentials file with a config.yml), and never print docker inspect without a format filter

## What a fix can break

Nothing, as long as the new environment file is in place before the restart.

Run `stackward explain CF-004` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
